solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Month getting stuffed with endless rehashed Gore gibberish

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the following name is cut off
a thing stuffed with something has it packed inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
rehashing old material serves it up again in a new arrangement

parts.note: Al Gore's surname without its last letter, before being reshuffled

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on Al Gore recycling the same old speeches, padded out into nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The three remaining letters of Gore are rearranged and stuffed between the first two and last letter of the month abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialist language that sounds like meaningless gibberish to an outsider.

clue.text: see 5dn.
(& 9ac.) John's sort of schoolboy repartee?

parts.note: surface reading: the kind of witty comeback a boy called John goes in for at school
setter's reading: a john is slang for a toilet, so the repartee is the toilet-joke kind schoolboys love

explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a schoolboy's name; in American slang a john is a toilet, which points to jokes about bodily functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet jokes are the classic juvenile comedy of the playground, so this phrase names exactly that brand of wit.

clue.text: Was a viewer supplied with your organ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: looked at something, past tense of a verb of watching
second meaning: having the organ of sight, as in blue-whatever

explanation.walkthrough: In a Private Eye clue 'your organ' sounds rude, but the organ meant is the one you are reading with.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of the verb meaning to look at and an adjective for having a particular kind of eye.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Climax that hurt inside of Paddy (not the first)

indicators.note: the opening letter of the politician's surname is dropped
one piece sits inside the other, packed within it

parts.note: Paddy Ashdown, Liberal Democrat leader, by his surname less its first letter
the cry you make when something hurts

explanation.surface: Something painful happening inside an Irishman at the height of an encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like a generic Irishman, but it is Paddy Ashdown, the Liberal Democrat leader of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is the decisive final confrontation, the climax of a dispute or story.

clue.text: Representative Tim became sick embracing Labour's leader

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one piece goes inside the other
something sick is out of sorts, so these letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Labour MP called Tim fell ill while hugging the party leader, a typical moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblematic means symbolic or typical, so it serves as a synonym of representative in the sense of standing for something.

clue.text: Leader of Tories: run aground, floored, in decline

indicators.note: a ship run aground is wrecked, so the letters are knocked out of order
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: knocked to the floor, as a boxer is

explanation.surface: A grim report on the Tory leader: the party has hit the rocks and been knocked flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A turndown is a refusal or downturn, so it works as a noun synonym for a decline.

clue.text: Wood possibly scores holding one — pig!

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: scores in the sense of a great number

explanation.surface: Somebody marks a set of results and, finding one candidate rubbish, calls them a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' admits that the answer is only one kind of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish tropical timber, an example of wood.

clue.text: see 3dn.
Things to do: 1) Getting low-down on duck's arse

parts.note: a list's first item, often labelled a
gen is British slang for inside information
DA, the abbreviation of duck's arse, a 1950s quiffed hairstyle

explanation.surface: A to-do list whose first item is getting the gossip on a greaser's haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck's arse is the slicked-back teddy-boy haircut, usually shortened to DA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is literally a list of items to be dealt with, Latin for things that must be done.

clue.text: Lots of bucks set about beginning to deflower Heather Mooning

indicators.note: turned about, so the word runs the opposite way

parts.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: Rich men plotting to seduce a woman called Heather Mooning.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather Mooning reads as a woman's name, but both words are pieces: ling is common heather, and mooning is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooning about means idling aimlessly, the same as wasting time by lingering.

clue.text: Kill Nick and Roger!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to steal, British slang; it also means to have sex with, as roger does

explanation.walkthrough: Nick and Roger look like two men; they are slang verbs, to nick being to steal and to roger to have sex with, both senses of this phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrasal verb is slang for murdering, for stealing, and for having sex with somebody.

clue.text: Charles, coming out with rot, was once a thorn in Blair's side

definitions.text: was once a thorn in Blair's side

indicators.note: coming out of their usual order, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prince Charles talking nonsense used to annoy Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Labour cabinet minister who resigned over the Iraq war and was a persistent critic of Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a famously outspoken Labour minister who kept attacking her own prime minister, a constant irritant.

clue.text: Fine utterances made by Archer which give access to the prick?

definitions.text: which give access to the prick?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed for perjury

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer's speeches provoke a crude joke about him.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is Jeffrey Archer, jailed in 2001 for lying in court; prick is vulgar slang for the penis.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser flies are the opening at the front of trousers, giving access to what is inside.

clue.text: The place for MPs to get end away, Wimbledon?

indicators.note: sending the end away removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: the House of Commons, where MPs sit

explanation.surface: Where randy MPs go to have sex: Wimbledon perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: To get your end away is British slang for having sex, but here it cuts the end letter. Wimbledon Common is a large open space in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon has a famous common, an area of public open land, so it is an example with a question mark.

clue.text: Prepared cola nut and pig stuffing

indicators.note: ingredients that are prepared are chopped and mixed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stuffing of cola nut and pork.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffing looks like the recipe's filling; it is vulgar slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing is crude slang for having sex, a synonym of copulating.

clue.text: Pisspoor dim rival introduced as follower of Boris

indicators.note: something piss-poor is badly made, so these letters are badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
put in, as in introduced into something

explanation.surface: A dismal, stupid rival is brought in to succeed Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is Boris Yeltsin, Russia's president until 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: He succeeded Yeltsin as Russian president, so he literally followed him in office.

clue.text: Little woman needs her support with balls-inverting sex aid

parts.note: Vi, short for Violet or Victoria
a bra supports a woman's breasts

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a small woman, her bra and a sex toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' means nonsense, not testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibrator is a sex toy, an aid to sexual pleasure.

clue.text: 'Muscles' has flipping whopper — go down with assistance!

indicators.note: something flipped over is turned around, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A gym-goer nicknamed Muscles has told a huge lie and needs help to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down with assistance' hints at a sexual sense, but means descending a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a cliff on a rope, going down with its help.

clue.text: Dotty said ice cream might help fill a small jug

definitions.text: might help fill a small jug

indicators.note: said means as spoken, so the word is given by its sound

explanation.surface: A batty woman explains how an ice cream fills a little milk jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for a breast; implants are made of this material.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone is used in breast implants, which enlarge a small breast, here called a jug.

clue.text: One mad to give you head after noon, say?

definitions.text: One mad to give you head

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first one

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: An oral-sex offer made after midday.
explanation.walkthrough: To give you head looks like oral sex, but to nut someone is to headbutt them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutter is a crazy person, the sort who might headbutt you.

clue.text: Thatcher clobbered (with tip of elbow, not handbag) a piss-taker

indicators.note: something clobbered is knocked about, so the letters are scrambled
not means a letter is removed
'tip of' keeps only the first letter of 'elbow'

parts.note: H as the first letter of handbag, Thatcher's famous accessory, taken away

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher being hit, with a strike that isn't her handbag, by someone mocking her.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss-taker normally mocks people; here it means a tube that literally takes urine out.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a tube that drains urine from the bladder, so it literally takes piss away.

clue.text: Place for stiff one before start of Baltic Cruise

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: the first name of the actor Tom Cruise

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An erection before a cruise on the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, not an erection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a burial vault, the resting place of a corpse.

clue.text: Labour's last uncertainty: time for a split

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is the one taken

explanation.surface: Labour's final doubts lead the party towards a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a break in a relationship or party, a division or schism.

clue.text: Solid end removed from surgical appliance — Tony disheartened

indicators.note: with the end taken off, the word loses its final letter
with the heart taken out, the middle letter is lost

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, with a truss removed, is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty means reliable and dependable, so it shares a sense of solid.

clue.text: Girl clutching length, it gives rigidity to one's member

definitions.text: it gives rigidity to one's member

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tight, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A girl grasping something stiff and long.
explanation.walkthrough: Member suggests the penis; it means a limb, here the forearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the bones of the forearm, which keep that limb rigid.

clue.text: Brown accepting alternative work backing is "organised persecution"

indicators.note: going backwards, so the assembled letters read in reverse order
accepting something is taking it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the letters the parse needs for Brown; their source is unclear
op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown taking on an alternative job is described as a witch-hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: the two letters for Brown are what the reversal needs, but no standard abbreviation explains them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre or persecution of a minority, originally of Jews in Russia.

clue.text: Fellow nancies buggered backs

indicators.note: something buggered is broken, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deliberately crude sexual line about effeminate men.
explanation.walkthrough: Backs is the verb, as a sponsor backs a project.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance is to fund, so it supplies money, matching the verb backs.
